# Convert WebP to JPG

- Route: `/tools/convert-webp-to-jpg`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `image`
- Slug: `convert-webp-to-jpg`

## Summary

Turn WebP images into broadly compatible JPG files that work in any image viewer or editor. (Image tools)

## Details

WebP is great for the web — but older software, presentation tools, and printers often can't read it. Media Manipulator converts WebP back to JPG so you can use the image anywhere. Pick the quality you want, and we handle the rest.
### What it does
- Converts any .webp image (still or animated frame) to standard .jpg.
- Lets you choose JPG quality — higher quality = larger file.
- Flattens transparency over a chosen background color (JPG has no alpha channel).
- Preserves color profile when possible.
### How to use it
1. Upload WebP: Drop in a .webp file from your computer.
2. Pick JPG quality: 85 is a good default; lower for smaller files.
3. Encode JPG: ImageMagick re-encodes with the chosen quality.
4. Download JPG: Save a universally compatible .jpg file.
### Technical details
- Quality 85 is a long-standing balance point — anything above ~92 mostly just increases file size with little visual improvement.
- JPG has no transparency, so transparent WebPs are flattened. If you need transparency, convert to PNG instead.
- For lossless image conversion or animated WebPs, prefer PNG (still) or animated GIF.
### Use cases
- Sending photos to clients: Ensure the recipient can open the file on any device.
- Embedding in presentations: PowerPoint/Keynote slides accept JPG everywhere; WebP is hit-or-miss.
- Printing and photo labs: Most labs accept JPG only.
- Stock photo submissions: Many stock sites require JPG uploads.
### FAQ
Q: What about transparency?
A: JPG does not support transparency. Transparent WebPs are flattened against the chosen background color. If you need transparency, convert to PNG instead.
Q: What quality should I use?
A: 85 is a balanced default. Use 90+ for photos where quality matters most, 70 for thumbnails or previews.
Q: Will it work with animated WebP?
A: Only the first frame becomes a JPG. For animated WebP, convert to an animated GIF instead.
Q: Can I batch-convert multiple files?
A: The free tool handles one file at a time. Convert each WebP individually for now.
